title: 6.1.4 Lab: The aim line on the table
description: Put the aim line on a table with rails, so the line is the shot you are about to take.
unit: 6.1 Pocket: plan and the aim line

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The cue ball sits on the table and the rails hold it. There is no line.

steps.title: The line, on a table
steps.instructions: Add the same held-pointer line as the sub-build, from the cue ball to the pointer. Keep it inside `if (mouse.pressing())`.

steps.title: Check it reads as a shot
steps.instructions: Pull toward a rail and away from it: the line should always start at the cue ball and end under the pointer.
hints: A line that starts at the pointer and ends at the ball looks the same but reads backwards when you add power.

requirements.title: The line starts at the cue ball
requirements.description: The line begins at the cue ball and ends at the pointer, inside a press test. Help: 6.1.2 (Reading: The pointer: press, hold, let go)

requirements.title: The pull is shown
requirements.description: The distance from the ball to the pointer is shown. Help: 6.1.2 (Reading: The pointer: press, hold, let go)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: The aim line on the table". The task: draw an aim line from the cue ball to the pointer while the mouse is held, on a table with rails, and show the pull distance. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Line from the ball
rubric.description: The line uses the cue ball position and the pointer, inside a press test.

rubric.title: It is a shot, not a cursor
rubric.description: The line starts at the ball, not at the pointer.
